A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and another computer on the internet. Everything you send goes through that tunnel, scrambled so nobody in between can read it.

Here's the simple flow:

Your device scrambles (encrypts) your traffic.
It travels to the VPN company's computer.
That computer unscrambles it and talks to the website for you.

So the website sees the VPN's address, not yours. Your Wi-Fi owner or internet provider only sees scrambled data going to the VPN. It's handy on public Wi-Fi, but it doesn't make you invisible: the VPN company can still see your activity, so pick one you trust.
